architecture.approach: Four additive, default-off modules added to the existing wirekit crate: angi (parser and importer, no network), google_lsa (LSA over OAuth2 reusing wirekit::google_oauth), sage_intacct (XML gateway limited to three entities), and adp (REST over OAuth2 client credentials). No new crate, no new workspace member, no root manifest change (CON-101, CON-103, CON-104). Every module reuses wirekit core for the client, retry, rate limit, tracing, secret type, and WirekitError; no module depends on another. Each live module takes a base URL at construction so it is addressable by a sandbox without partner access. angi ships first because it has no network dependency; adp ships last because its payroll reconcile semantics carry the highest cost of being wrong.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/angi.rs
components.description: AngiLead, AngiLeadParser, AngiImport, ParseError, and the deterministic dedupe key. Parses caller-supplied email and CSV bytes only; adds no HTTP client for Angi.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/google_lsa.rs
components.description: GoogleLsaClient, Lead, Booking, LeadStatus. Reuses wirekit::google_oauth for refresh, maps 403 to an explicit account-not-approved variant, dedupes by lead ID, and never assumes a webhook.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/sage_intacct.rs
components.description: SageIntacctClient, Customer, Invoice, JournalEntry, ReportRequest. Derives success from the gateway status and errno, holds the sender password in the wirekit secret type, and bounds XML bytes and depth.

components.name: crates/wirekit/src/adp.rs
components.description: AdpClient, Employee, TimeCard, PayrollRun, PayrollReport, SubmissionOutcome. Caches a client-credentials token, preserves correlation IDs, redacts SSN and pay rates, and returns an unknown outcome for a payroll timeout instead of resubmitting.

dataModel.flowDescription: Caller constructs one client per tenant with its own credentials and optional base URL. Each call builds a typed request, delegates transport, retry, rate-limit, and tracing to wirekit core, then maps the provider response into a typed model or a WirekitError. The Angi module never performs I/O: it takes bytes the caller already has and returns AngiLead values plus per-row outcomes. Nothing is persisted; every model is returned to the caller and dropped or stored by the consuming application.

securityConsiderations.description: CON-511 and CON-519 expanded: credentials arrive at construction, are held in the wirekit secret type, are never embedded or defaulted, and no module reads a .env file. Rotation is possible because nothing caches a credential beyond the client instance.
CON-512 expanded: tenant isolation is structural. One client per tenant, no module-level cache or static, and no shared token or response store, so concurrent tenants cannot observe each other.
CON-514 expanded: a per-provider token bucket from wirekit core, with caller override, and a tracing metric on every rate-limit hit.
CON-515 expanded: email bodies, CSV rows, JSON leads, XML gateway responses, and ADP error arrays are all untrusted input and produce typed errors rather than panics or silent defaults.
CON-214 and CON-211 expanded: request start, finish, retry, rate-limit, and error are traced; the sender password, SSN, and pay rates are redacted and their types do not implement Serialize.
CON-520 enforced through the https-only base URL check, and CON-201/CON-202 kept in force: forbid(unsafe_code), deny(missing_docs), one rustdoc comment per public item.
CON-516 recorded as NOT APPLICABLE: no database, cache, or query surface exists in these modules, so there is no injection vector to parameterise.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Byte and nesting-depth ceilings are configuration-driven and enforced before or during parse: XML for Intacct, CSV row and file size for Angi, response size for LSA and ADP.
Validation happens before allocation grows: parse into a bounded structure, then map into a model, so a hostile body cannot force unbounded allocation.
One tracing event per request stage, not per field, and redacted values are never formatted into the event, so tracing cost stays flat with payload size.
Retry backoff is bounded to three attempts with jitter, so a failing provider cannot hold a caller for an unbounded time.

risks.description: A new dependency brings a licence incompatible with MIT OR Apache-2.0.
risks.mitigation: Licence verified before adding; both dependencies are feature-gated, so removal is cheap.

risks.description: Provider endpoint paths are invented from memory.
risks.mitigation: The plan fixes the contract only; paths are confirmed from provider documentation at apply and recorded in rustdoc.

risks.description: Partner access is denied for LSA, ADP, or Intacct.
risks.mitigation: Every live module is sandbox-addressable, so the contract is implementable without access.

risks.description: A payroll submission is retried after a timeout and double-pays.
